chunks: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform the zuhr prayer at a dhira', and the 'asr prayer at approximately that. If it is said: the reports which indicate that the beginning of the time is more virtuous are general, and there is no specification in them for the time that you mentioned, then from where did you say that, and why did you not apply them according to their generality? It is said to him: we understood that according to what we have said so that the reports would not contradict one another, and there have also come reports explaining it.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more virtuous or superior in merit
key_terms.أَوَّلَ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning of the prayer time
key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the zuhr prayer, the midday obligatory salat
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ: the hadith reports or transmitted narrations
key_terms.الْعَصْرَ: the 'asr prayer, the afternoon obligatory salat
key_terms.الْعُمُومِ: generality, applying the wording without restriction

ai.seo_question: How are general hadiths about the virtue of praying at the beginning of prayer time reconciled with specific reports on zuhr and 'asr timing?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the timing of zuhr and 'asr prayer and cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also explains a juristic method of reconciling general narrations about the virtue of praying at the beginning of the time with more specific reports that clarify the intended timing.
